submitter: 283/RFC_032 §10 building thread, Half B ROUND 2 (2026-08-24) — the disputed refusal is WITHDRAWN and contained; resubmitted on the same correlation
rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 came back REVISE on a gating HIGH from `guardian`: converting this shared render seam's log-only defect path into a hard error is new authority shipped unconditional, licensed only by a census of today's callers — "a census of TODAY's live templates cannot bound tomorrow's caller; this needs an explicit council sign-off on the authority question, not a footnote."

**I am not re-arguing it with better measurements.** This estate has litigated this exact shape once: RFC_044 shipped default-ON behaviour on two shared render actions, drew the same HIGH, and was VETOED next round with "routing a scope objection to architecture review does not license deploying the disputed change". The owner ruling of 2026-07-28 says the same. So the disputed half is WITHDRAWN and the authority question goes to the owner as RFC_050, with the blast-radius data already gathered and four answers costed.

WHAT REPLACED IT, AND WHY IT IS NOT A RETREAT TO THE LOG. `RenderTemplate` now PUBLISHES `RenderContext.UnboundInstanceToken`. This is the fix for `editquality`'s medium, which was the sharper objection: I cited the owner ruling at component_library.go:1216 ("a named log is NOT escalation") as licence to REFUSE, and that ruling's own remedy ON THIS FUNCTION was to PUBLISH — `ctx.AbsentRequiredFields` — precisely because the seam has no database handle and no site identity, so it publishes and a caller with both acts. Following the precedent I quoted means doing what it did. The new field sits beside it and copies its shape, and it is strictly more than the log it replaced because a log is not readable by code.

THE CLAIM GUARDIAN ASKED ME TO EVIDENCE WAS WRONG AS STATED, AND IS NOW CORRECTED. I asserted "every caller already handles this error channel correctly since bugs_open/260" without checking per-caller. Read 2026-08-24: of the 7 call sites that can reach an {{.InstanceID}} template, 6 fail loudly and ONE does not — `rerender_page_sections_action.go:661` CARRIES the stored HTML and continues, deliberately, because that action IS the repair vehicle. Two further callers soften a render error and cannot reach such a template (chrome census 0). The contract was never uniform. Full table in the code comment and RFC_050 §3.

AND I INTRODUCED THE VERY DEFECT THIS FILE'S LANDMINE WARNS ABOUT. `reuse_agent` and `debug_historian` both objected that `instanceaudit` classified the new refusal with `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "rendered EMPTY")`, citing the standing landmine that a converter's refusal REASON is a routing signal callers grep for. Correct. Now `ErrEmptyElementID` + `errors.Is`, mutation-proven BOTH ways: rewording the message must still pass, and dropping the `%w` wrap must fail. Checked before adding it — no other caller string-matches this function, so the sentinel lands before the pattern spreads rather than after.

THE LINT CHANGE IS FULLY REVERTED and this is containment paying for itself: the skip existed only because a REFUSAL turned the absence probe into an error. With a report there is no error, the probe works, the ~140 components keep their coverage (`bug_historian`), and there is now only one change in this submission rather than two separable ones (`guardian`, low).

plan.summary: WITHDRAW the render-seam refusal and publish RenderContext.UnboundInstanceToken instead; add the same report to the second render path; make the gate's empty-id refusal a typed sentinel routed with errors.Is; revert the lint change, now unnecessary; file RFC_050 for the authority question. The EmptyElementIDs detector class and the gate branch from round 1 are unchanged.

The field's declaration carries its own kill instruction: if RFC_050 is answered 'do not arm', DELETE it rather than leave a reader-less field to rot, which is the cost the 2026-07-29 ruling names.

A report ON the path is the guard a census cannot be. Log-only here because there is no RenderContext to publish onto, which is itself why RFC_050's question is scoped to BOTH paths rather than treating this one as done.

reuse_agent + debug_historian, same round, both citing this function's own landmine about refusal reasons being routing signals. I created that dependency while holding the entry that warns about it. The sentinel's doc comment records the census that licenses adding it now: all five non-test callers branch on `err != nil` and the needsJudged bool, and the one that formats %v puts it in a human issues list, not a routing decision — so nothing existing breaks and the pattern is stopped early.

edits.rationale: What the architecture seat asked for by name, and what guardian's 'explicit sign-off, not a footnote' requires. Four answers costed (publish-only / unconditional / opt-in via the existing enforce_instance_scope key / refuse only on the two ungated live-page routes), the per-caller table, the blast-radius census, and §5 on why this is not simply 'add a default-OFF switch' — the 2026-07-29 and 2026-08-02 rulings point opposite ways here, which is why it needs a human.

The publish test asserts the FIELD, not the log — a log is not readable by code, which is the whole reason the field exists, so asserting the log would pin the thing that was already insufficient. Two positive controls (a bound render must not set it; a template that never spells the token must not set it) so it cannot pass against a flag set unconditionally. The sentinel test reworders the message and requires routing to survive, and requires a DIFFERENT hard refusal not to match.

The mutation control now asserts BOTH halves of what containment leaves — the seam publishes, and the bytes it still returns collide. Keeping both is deliberate: the flag alone would pass against a future change that started returning safe output; the collision alone would let the publication rot. ALSO RESTORES a test my own round-2 edit destroyed — a scripted edit overran and swallowed TestTemplateNeedsInstanceID_… and every check I ran (build, suite, gofmt, verify-head-builds --test) stayed GREEN over the hole, because deleting a test removes assertions rather than breaking anything. Caught by the pre-commit architecture signal one commit later; filed in WRONG_CALLS with the one-line inventory-diff check that would have caught it, now in the runbook.

plan.risks:
1. THE CONTAINED STATE HAS A REAL COST AND I AM NOT HIDING IT: `UnboundInstanceToken` currently has NO READER. A field nothing consumes is exactly the mechanism-rot the 2026-07-29 owner ruling warns about, and it is why RFC_050 needs answering rather than filing. The kill instruction is at the field's declaration: if the answer is 'do not arm', DELETE it. Meanwhile the section editor can still write id="" to a live page — that damage is NOT fixed by this submission, only made visible.
2. NEITHER RENDER PATH ENFORCES NOW. Round 1 enforced on one and not the other, which bug_historian correctly named as the 016b §9 shape; round 2 reports on both and enforces on neither, which is symmetric but weaker. If the council prefers enforcement on the two ungated live-page routes today (RFC_050 answer (d)) rather than waiting for the owner, say so and I will build it in round 3 — it is two call sites, both of which already refuse on a render error.
3. I DESTROYED A TEST IN THIS ROUND AND EVERY CHECK I RAN SAID IT WAS FINE. A scripted edit overran and swallowed TestTemplateNeedsInstanceID_matchesTheSpellingsGoAccepts; build, suite, gofmt and verify-head-builds --test all passed over the hole, because deleting a test removes assertions rather than breaking anything. Restored verbatim, filed in WRONG_CALLS, and the one-line inventory-diff check is in the runbook. Flagged HERE because it bears on how much weight a seat should give my 'all tests pass' claims: the correct weight is 'the tests that ran, passed'.
4. THE DETECTOR IS STILL A REGEX SCAN (unchanged from round 1). reEmptyElementID matches id="" inside a comment or a JS string too; it errs toward reporting, and the corpus says it reports nothing today.
5.
